solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Consider putting stick in river

indicators.note: putting one thing in another tells us the stick goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another on the Welsh border
a bat is a stick for striking a ball

explanation.surface: Someone muses on poking a stick into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate a question is to consider or weigh it, a plain synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Sad three months in America, bringing collapse

parts.note: feeling down means feeling sad
Americans call autumn the fall, a season of about three months

explanation.surface: A gloomy season in the States brings someone's ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a ruin or sudden fall from power, a synonym for collapse.

clue.text: Report on New Delhi, as Asian

parts.note: a report can be a loud noise, such as a bang

indicators.note: new here means remade, so the letters of Delhi and as are formed afresh

explanation.surface: A news report about New Delhi, viewed as part of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the city name but is the anagram signal; DELHI AS rearranged gives LADESHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bangladeshi is a person from Bangladesh in South Asia, an example of an Asian.

clue.text: Going this way and that, hit the horn

indicators.note: reading in either direction gives the same letters, so the word works both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A driver weaving about the road leans on the horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: 'Going this way and that' says it reads identically forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To toot is to sound a car horn briefly, a verb synonym for honking.

clue.text: General swine booked by Orwell?

definitions.meaning: the French emperor Bonaparte was a famous military commander
the ruling pig in George Orwell's novel Animal Farm bears this name

explanation.surface: A military man is insulted as a pig in Orwell's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was a celebrated general, and Orwell named his tyrant pig in Animal Farm after him.

clue.text: Similar thing mixing guano with ale

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters of guano and ale together into a new order

explanation.surface: An unappetising recipe blends bird droppings with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogue is something comparable or parallel to another thing, so a similar thing.

clue.text: Where a chimney stack is free

definitions.meaning: a chimney stack sits literally up on the roof of a home
an idiom for something given without charge, as a drink from the landlord

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about rooftops that also means no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the stack's position atop a dwelling; idiomatically, paid for by the establishment, hence free.

clue.text: Special time, time for tea by all conclusions

indicators.note: conclusions are the ends of words, so take the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Teatime treated as a special occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinctive period of history, a special stretch of time.

clue.text: Lower number after last of ten

indicators.note: after places the anaesthetic word behind the letter taken from ten
last of points to the final letter of the word ten

parts.note: read as numb-er: something that numbs, as ether did as an early anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A figure placed below ten in a count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, the anaesthetic ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old adjective meaning lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Where one's heading for Nairobi in important African capital?

definitions.text: Where one's heading for Nairobi in important African capital?

indicators.note: in places the letter from Nairobi inside the word for important

parts.note: key means crucial or important

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
a capital letter is the initial one, here of African

explanation.surface: A traveller bound for Nairobi wonders which country they are in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Nairobi is the capital of this African nation, so anyone heading for Nairobi is going there.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of the East African nation, so it is where a traveller to Nairobi goes.

clue.text: Appealing, don't always expect success?

definitions.meaning: charming or engaging in a sweet way
from the saying you ..., you lose some

explanation.surface: Advice that charm won't always bring victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means attractive and charming; split in two it echoes the proverb about winning some and losing some.

clue.text: Draw a measure of land on back of packet

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here of packet

parts.note: a tract is an expanse or area of land

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a land survey on the back of a packet.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, a verb synonym meaning pull in.

clue.text: Turn over paper — to find pen

definitions.meaning: to crease a sheet so one part lies over the other
an enclosure for sheep on a farm

explanation.surface: Turning a page to find a writing pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease paper over on itself, and also a sheep enclosure; both senses share the word.

clue.text: Unfortunately easterly borders shut, open one of three sides

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went awry, so the letters are jumbled
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Border posts in the east have closed, alas, and one side opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' gives EY, the outer letters of easterly; with SHUT and OPEN these ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In a right-angled triangle the longest side, opposite the right angle, is one of its three sides.

clue.text: Appalling madman in blue, a misfit

indicators.note: in tells us the madman sits inside the jumbled letters
a misfit is out of place, so the letters of blue and a are disordered

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A crazed man dressed in blue looks out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misfit' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; nutter is British slang for a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Unutterable means too dreadful to be spoken of, an intensifier close to appalling.

clue.text: Used ticker?

definitions.meaning: a clock's thin hand counting seconds, which ticks round

explanation.definitionFit: Means not new, already owned; literally also the clock hand that ticks off seconds.

clue.text: Bag of liquid not opening — some help to a fireman!

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the bladder is the body's sac holding urine

explanation.surface: A water bag that won't open is little use to a firefighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Firefighters climb extending ladders to reach high windows, so one is a helpful tool for them.

clue.text: Report of traffic jam, one read by a newsreader, say?

definitions.text: one read by a newsreader, say?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a queue of autos, that is cars, is a traffic jam

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin about a traffic jam, read out by the presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTO QUEUE, a line of cars, said aloud gives the trade name.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the prompting screen from which a television presenter reads the script.

clue.text: Letter like O

definitions.meaning: a printed notice sent to many people at once
round in shape, as the letter O is

explanation.definitionFit: A mass-mailed notice is a circular, and something round in shape like an O is circular.

clue.text: Margate about to welcome second A-lister

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece is placed inside the other
about suggests moving around, so the letters of Margate are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Kent seaside town of Margate rolls out the red carpet for a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MARGATE into MEGATAR, which takes in S.
explanation.definitionFit: An A-lister is a top celebrity, and a megastar is a hugely famous performer.

clue.text: Country is one with a capital in Tallinn, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged another way
the capital of a word is its first letter, here the initial of Tallinn

explanation.surface: A country identified by Tallinn being its capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital in Tallinn' gives T; with IS ONE and A it is rearranged. The surface is a fair clue too: Tallinn is the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic nation whose capital city is Tallinn is a country in northern Europe.

clue.text: Bloodsucker declines to penetrate outer parts of tissue

indicators.note: penetrating means going inside, so one piece goes within the other
the outer parts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the sun sets or declines as it goes down

explanation.surface: Waning forces push into the edges of body tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: The African tsetse fly feeds on blood and spreads sleeping sickness, an example of a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Look to find power in a faction

indicators.note: in places the power letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sect is a breakaway group or faction
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Search for strength within a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect and look both mean appearance, as in the aspect or look of a place.

clue.text: The two things together on top of yellow shed

parts.note: both means the two together, one and the other

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pair of items placed on top of something yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a basic hut or shelter in Scotland, a small shed-like building.

clue.text: Make PG a PR man?

parts.note: a doctor is a GP, and spinning that pair round turns the letters into PG

explanation.surface: A publicist is asked to make something suitable for family viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: spin a doctor (GP) and you make PG. PG is the film rating for parental guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a public-relations agent who puts a favourable slant on news.

clue.text: Island lacking shopping centre a killer in the main

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a piece is taken away

parts.note: Mallorca is a Spanish island in the Mediterranean
a mall is an American-style shopping centre

explanation.surface: A holiday island without its mall, and a killer at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale hunts in the open sea; the main is poetic for the ocean.

clue.text: Arm supporter in Dublin bar, every second counting

indicators.note: every second means take alternate letters, starting from the second one

explanation.surface: A drinker propped up at an Irish pub, counting the seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones, part of the arm's skeleton that supports it.

clue.text: Closely observe label designed to grab you

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it, so one piece is held within the other
designed means arranged anew, so the letters of label are reworked

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: An eye-catching label designed to seize your attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns LABEL into EBALL, which grabs YE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them closely, an informal synonym for scrutinise.

clue.text: Australian grounded in dance music

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of dance music

explanation.surface: An Aussie stays rooted in dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless emu is a large Australian bird that cannot leave the ground.

clue.text: A party in shed that's flat in the main

indicators.note: in places the party pieces inside the shed

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
Lib is short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A gathering held in a shed that falls flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of the sea; the main is poetic for the ocean.

clue.text: Stormy in truth under Yeltsin

indicators.note: in shows the letters run inside the words truth under Yeltsin

explanation.surface: Turbulent times for truth in Yeltsin's Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that is thundery brings thunder and storms, so it is a synonym for stormy.

clue.text: Speed always on wheels

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the always word follows

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Always driving fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along headlong, a verb synonym for speed.
